extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation. It assesses five core dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark emphasizes realism by curating datasets across diverse embodiments, attribute-rich objects, multi-view scenes, and memory-driven navigation, drawing from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection. RoboBench introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator evaluation framework to assess long-horizon planning by simulating whether predicted plans achieve critical object-state changes under physical and visual constraints, enabling faithful assessment of embodied feasibility.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.publisher: State Key Laboratory of Multimedia Information Processing, School of Computer Science, Peking University; Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence; Institute for Brain and Intelligence, Fudan University; University of Science and Technology Beijing; Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics
extraction.citeAs: RoboBench: A Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Models as Embodied Brains
extraction.rai:dataCollection: RoboBench curates datasets from large-scale real robotic data and in-house collection, ensuring realism by spanning diverse embodiments (single-arm, dual-arm, mobile manipulator, humanoid robot), attribute-rich objects (material, physical properties, world knowledge), multi-view scenes (including occlusion), and memory-driven navigation. The data collection process involves preprocessing, annotation with VLMs, detection models, or human experts, and Q&A format generation, tailored for each dimension (instruction, perception, planning, affordance, failure analysis).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: RoboBench draws from large-scale real robotic datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment Collaboration et al. (2023), Fang et al. (2023), Collaboration et al. (2023), Liu et al. (2024c), Wu et al. (2024), Bu et al. (2025)) and in-house collection to ensure realism and reduce the sim-to-real gap. The raw data includes robotic videos, images, and annotations covering diverse embodiments, objects, and scenes.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: RoboBench applies both general and task-specific filters during data construction, including image quality checks, task validity rules (e.g., excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks), and post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators. Items solved by all models are removed, while items failed by all models undergo manual review and correction. The preprocessing pipeline includes standardization into multiple-choice QA formats, structured annotations (e.g., task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata), and mapping steps into function templates for planning tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations are created using a combination of VLMs (e.g., Gemini), detection models, and human experts. For perception tasks, fine-grained attributes (e.g., object properties, functional attributes) are extracted. For planning, structured annotations (e.g., task summaries, step-wise instructions, DAGs for dependencies) are generated and refined by humans. Affordance prediction involves annotating static (contact points), dynamic (motion trajectories), and navigation affordances. Failure analysis includes expert-labeled execution and planning errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: RoboBench employs a two-stage quality control process: data filtering during construction (general and task-specific criteria) and post-construction validation by 20 annotators. Items solved by all models are removed, while items failed by all models undergo manual review and correction. Majority-vote strategies are used to ensure linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1-3 (varies by task type: multiple-choice questions for perception/failure, structured plans for instruction/planning, point/trajectory predictions for affordance)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators conducted comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. Specific demographics (e.g., age, gender, expertise) are not provided in the paper.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini, Detection Models (e.g., for bounding boxes, segmentation), VLM-based annotation tools
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: RoboBench provides a leaderboard and systematic evaluation of SOTA MLLMs, offering actionable insights for advancing embodied brains. The benchmark is designed to be updated with new tasks, dimensions, and models, though specific versioning or deprecation policies are not detailed in the paper.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: RoboBench highlights fundamental limitations in current MLLMs, such as difficulties with implicit instruction comprehension, spatiotemporal reasoning, cross-scenario planning, fine-grained affordance understanding, and execution failure diagnosis. These findings underscore the need for more robust, generalizable embodied intelligence to address real-world robotic challenges.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: RoboBench acknowledges biases in current MLLMs, including weaknesses in implicit instruction grounding, robotic perception (e.g., robot-view recognition, temporal grounding), and long-horizon planning. The benchmark exposes disparities in performance across dimensions (e.g., perception reasoning vs. failure analysis) and embodiments (e.g., dual-arm coordination).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: RoboBench has several known limitations: (1) Limited task realism in some benchmarks (e.g., reliance on simulations or simplified scenarios). (2) Simplistic planning evaluation in prior works (e.g., multiple-choice or text similarity metrics). (3) Gaps in implicit instruction understanding, spatiotemporal reasoning, and failure diagnosis. (4) Performance disparities across dimensions and embodiments. Non-recommended uses include relying solely on symbolic matching for planning evaluation or ignoring physical/visual constraints in real-world robotic tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: RoboBench is designed for Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-Tuning of MLLMs as embodied brains. It provides a unified scaffold to quantify high-level cognition, clarify the role of the embodied brain, and guide the development of next-generation MLLMs for robotic manipulation. Usage guidelines emphasize evaluating models across five dimensions (instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, failure analysis) to uncover bottlenecks in embodied cognition.
